title: Redesigned chat cards
summary: Cards in Grok Bot chats have a new design with a cleaner layout, part of an update the team says improves quality, polish, and speed.

title: Refreshed look with a new typeface and themes
summary: Grok Bot has a refreshed look, with a new typeface and themes.

title: Grok Bot is much faster
summary: The Grok Bot team says computer tasks now finish 3x sooner on average, and replies to everything else arrive in less than half the time.

title: Faster, more reliable voice calls
summary: Voice calls with Grok Bot are faster, more reliable, and better at remembering past conversations.

title: Tag @bot on X to start a task
summary: Tag @bot in a post on X and Grok Bot gets to work on it.

title: Notifications only on the device you're using
summary: Grok Bot notifications now go only to the device you're using.

title: Grok Bot can read X Chat
summary: Grok Bot can now read X Chat. Connect X, then ask it to work across your messages.

title: Robinhood, Coinbase, Trello, and more connectors
summary: Grok Bot now connects to Robinhood, Coinbase, Trello, PostHog, beehiiv, eToro, and more. Teams can also now submit connectors to the Grok Bot marketplace.

title: Plugins can be submitted
summary: A Grok Bot team member shared that anyone can submit plugins for Grok Bot (and Grok and Cursor) through a public submission form.

title: Plus aliases for Grok Bot email
summary: Grok Bot email supports plus aliases: send and receive with dedicated aliases, or set routines that trigger only for mail sent to one alias.
corrected: 2026-10-17: confirmed by the official @bot account (https://x.com/bot/status/2111184278377857410), so the status changed from reported to confirmed.

title: Basecamp connector launched
summary: Basecamp announced an official Grok Bot connector, available from Connect Apps inside Grok Bot.

title: Grok Bot X Communities
summary: The team opened applications for curated Grok Bot group chats on X for GTM, product, marketing, engineering, recruiting, and design.

title: Weekly roundup video
summary: A team video walks through the week: Bot's own email, better X, Shopify, more color, email drafts, Bot's computer, template search, PR previews, routine right-clicks, and 5 new languages.

title: One plan for Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor, and X
summary: The X Subscription is one plan covering Cursor, Grok, Grok Bot, and X Premium. Every change is opt-in; if you do nothing, nothing changes.

title: Grok Bot gets its own email
summary: Bots can use their own email address to sign up for services, contact businesses for you, or schedule time with someone.

title: Shopify connector
summary: Connect Shopify, then ask Grok Bot to check orders, track inventory, and keep product listings up to date.

title: Search, read, and monitor X
summary: Grok Bot can now search, read, and monitor X.

title: Usage limits reset
summary: Usage limits were reset for all Grok Bot users.

title: Proactive suggestions
summary: Grok Bot can now suggest ways to help without you needing to ask.

title: Better for building software
summary: Bots can hand off coding tasks to Cursor, manage PRs with the GitHub and Origin plugins, and share video demos of what they build.

title: Finance integration
summary: Link bank, card, and investment accounts with the new Finance integration, then ask Grok Bot to help manage spending and investments.

title: Cleaner interface
summary: Quality-of-life update with a cleaner interface for working with your bots.

title: Voice notes
summary: Grok Bot can now send you voice notes.

title: Grok Bot can talk
summary: Grok Bot can now talk.

title: 1Password
summary: Grok Bot can use 1Password: share items in a vault, approve each fill, and the secrets stay in your password manager.

title: Uploads to Google Drive and OneDrive
summary: Version 0.53.0: Bots can upload files to Google Drive or OneDrive or attach them to a Gmail draft, and a Bot's computer now uses your time zone. The same release added 1Password sign-in on Mac (see the 1Password entry).

title: Search palette puts Bots and settings first
summary: Version 0.54.0: Cmd/Ctrl+K shows matching Bots, settings, actions, and routines before messages (quote a search to see every message), and iPhone HEIC photos show as images.

title: Regrouped setup checklist for teams
summary: A second Sep 16 release groups the dashboard Setup Checklist into Recommended and Optional, shows the build date in About, and fixes GitHub disconnect and some 1Password sign-in checks.

title: More GitHub actions for Bots
summary: Bots can work with GitHub releases, tags, labels, sub-issues, discussions, and collaborators, create branches, and submit one review across several files. Stopping a Bot also stops the Bots and Cloud Agents it started.

title: Bots can start a Project
summary: A Bot can start a Project when you ask: a Cloud Agent that plans the work and runs its own agents. Link previews also show real titles for private Notion, GitHub, and Slack links.

title: Five more languages and better screen reader support
summary: Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, and Norwegian Bokmål join the language list, screen readers announce more of the app, and a card explains when a usage limit, rate limit, or timeout stops a reply.

title: Busy Bots answer you first
summary: When you message a busy Bot, it answers you before working through queued updates from other Bots and agents. Expired Auto-review cards also offer Always allow, and Enterprise admins can store Team Secrets.

title: Team Bots for a whole team
summary: Version 0.61.0 adds Team Bots: publish one Bot for your team, and teammates chat with it in the app or Slack, each in their own conversation. Each teammate's use counts against their own allowance.

title: Email drafts work with Outlook
summary: A second Sep 26 release lets you review a Bot's new email in chat and send it from your Outlook account. Wide tables in Bot messages also scroll sideways instead of squeezing.

title: Quote text and start lists in the composer
summary: Select text and press Cmd/Ctrl+L to quote it, type - or 1. to start a list, and get spell check as you type. A Bot's info pane gains a Library tab of the pages, files, and links it has shared.

title: Approvals in Slack and clearer usage limits
summary: In Slack threads, a Bot that needs approval posts a Review an action card only you can answer. When included usage runs out, the app shows the usage limit notice instead of Bot failed to respond.

title: Refreshed avatars and Secure Form logins
summary: Version 0.64.0 refreshes Bot avatars with bigger eyes and new shapes, opens logins in a Secure Form window that names the site, and lets you turn off drafts for a Bot so it sends directly.

title: Voice chats with Team Bots, automatic updates on
summary: Version 0.65.0 lets teammates start a voice chat with a Team Bot and turns Automatic Updates on by default (you can turn it off in Settings, Updates).

title: Marketplace becomes Connect Apps
summary: An Oct 2 release renames Marketplace to Connect Apps, with category chips and Recommended for you first. Bot status lines use phrases like Thinking it through.

title: Five more languages and Gmail send-as drafts
summary: Version 0.68.0 adds Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Swahili, and Hausa, and lets email drafts go out from a verified Gmail send-as address, with a From picker if you have more than one.

title: Slide decks, formatted emails, and a bigger Bot screen
summary: Version 0.68.1: Bots build slide decks and deliver them as PowerPoint or Google Slides, send formatted emails from a draft card, and work on a 1920 × 1200 computer screen, up from 1280 × 800.

title: In-chat app cards, payments, and Find in page
summary: Version 0.70.2 (which includes 0.69.0 to 0.70.1): connectors like Figma, Notion, and Canva can show an interactive app card in chat, Bots can pay with X Money or Stripe Link, and Cmd/Ctrl+F opens Find in page.
